selectionGuide.description: An office comparison presents two labeled subjects before a built-in reaction dismisses any distinction between them.
bestFor: arguing that two supposedly different things are functionally equivalent
exposing a distinction as superficial or misleading
a sarcastic comparison whose punchline is sameness
avoidWhen: one option should clearly be preferred over the other
the relationship is cause and effect rather than equivalence
more than two subjects need independent treatment

mechanics.visual: The side-by-side subjects invite inspection, while the office reaction collapses the expected distinction into one verdict.
mechanics.text: Put one subject in left and the other in right using comparable noun phrases; the image already supplies the 'same picture' conclusion.
